nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean water and sanitation|Water purification techniques|Silver ionization disinfection_qna_000
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What year was it established that bacteria could transmit electrons externally to electrodes?
nodes.answer: It was established in 1999 that bacteria could transmit electrons externally to electrodes.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean water and sanitation|Water purification techniques|Silver ionization disinfection_qna_001
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What is the main purpose of the anode in MFCs?
nodes.answer: The main purpose of the anode is to encourage the establishment of biofilms and enhance the likelihood of extracellular electron transfer (EET), which is dependent on bacterial metabolic rates and electrode interfacial charge transfer efficiency.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean water and sanitation|Water purification techniques|Silver ionization disinfection_qna_002
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What was the procedure for photographing the juveniles?
nodes.answer: The juveniles were relaxed in a 1:1 solution of FSW and 7% MgCl2 before being photographed using a microscope.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean water and sanitation|Water purification techniques|Silver ionization disinfection_qna_003
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What is the main material discussed in the paragraph and what properties does it have?
nodes.answer: The main material discussed is AgNP (silver nanoparticles), which have enhanced antimicrobial efficacy at nanoscale dimensions of less than 100 nm.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean water and sanitation|Water purification techniques|Silver ionization disinfection_qna_004
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: What are the largest markets for silver nanoparticles according to the paragraph?
nodes.answer: The largest markets for silver nanoparticles are medical applications (24%), followed by textiles (17.6%), cosmetics (13.4%), and home appliances (9.4%).

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean water and sanitation|Water purification techniques|Silver ionization disinfection_qna_005
nodes.label: Ethics and regulation
nodes.question: What has led to the restriction on the use of nanosilver in products that contact food or the human body?
nodes.answer: The negative impacts on the human body have led to the establishment of the European Union Directive 2002/72/EC, which governs the migration and release rates of silver nanoparticles into food and water.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean water and sanitation|Water purification techniques|Silver ionization disinfection_qna_006
nodes.label: Taxonomy
nodes.question: What are the different methods to synthesize silver nanoparticles (AgNPs)?
nodes.answer: Silver nanoparticles can be synthesized using physical routes, wet chemistry, or bio-based syntheses.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean water and sanitation|Water purification techniques|Silver ionization disinfection_qna_007
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What was the purpose of carbonizing Dicranopteris pedata in the study?
nodes.answer: The purpose of carbonizing Dicranopteris pedata was to characterize it and test its performance in removing Pb(II).

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean water and sanitation|Water purification techniques|Silver ionization disinfection_qna_008
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What method is used to analyze the particle composition before and after the scrubber in this study?
nodes.answer: The study employs single-particle mass spectrometry using laser desorption/ionization (LDI) and laser desorption/resonance-enhanced multiphoton ionization (LD/REMPI) techniques to analyze the particle components.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean water and sanitation|Water purification techniques|Silver ionization disinfection_qna_009
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What method is used to analyze the individual particles and provide chemical profiles in the study?
nodes.answer: The study utilizes a single-particle mass spectrometer that employs laser desorption/ionization (LDI) and laser desorption/resonance-enhanced multiphoton ionization (LD/REMPI) to analyze the individual particles and provide their chemical profiles.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean water and sanitation|Water purification techniques|Silver ionization disinfection_qna_010
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What technique was used to analyze the composition of particles before and after the scrubber?
nodes.answer: A single-particle mass spectrometer was used to analyze the composition of particles before and after the scrubber, providing chemical insights at the single-particle level.
